title: Idempotent vCenter content library item creation over Client-Token
prompt:
The vcenter_content package provisions vSphere Content Library items on a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 vCenter. vcenter_content/client.py is a skeleton: the class and method signatures are there, the bodies are not. Implement them using only the Python standard library -- this ships inside an appliance image where pip install is not an option.

docs/contract.json is the contract this client is built against, derived from the vSphere Automation API OpenAPI document for vCenter. It names the three operations you may use and records the path, headers, security scheme and property rules for each; docs/official_sources.json records where it came from. Do not call an operation the contract does not name.

What ContentLibraryClient has to do:

1. Authenticate lazily and reuse one successful session. Cis.Session_create takes HTTP Basic credentials and returns a session token. If session creation returns a 503, retry it as described below. Once a token has been obtained, every other operation authenticates by sending that token in the vmware-api-session-id header and must not resend the Basic credentials. Reuse the token for the lifetime of the client instance.

2. Create a library item idempotently. ensure_library_item() calls Content.Library.Item_create and returns the new item's identifier. This is a mutating call over an unreliable link, so the server can commit the item and still fail to answer -- a naive retry would create a second one. The spec provides the Client-Token header for exactly this: a UUID that makes creation idempotent. Retrying must not be able to leave a duplicate item behind, including when the retries are exhausted. When the caller does not supply a token, generate one.

3. Retry only what is retryable. A 503 from either session creation or item creation is transient: retry up to max_attempts, sleeping backoff seconds between attempts. Every other documented status is terminal. Raise VCenterApiError carrying the HTTP status plus the error_type and messages from the Vapi.Std.Errors.Error body; exhausted retries raise it too.

4. Send the body the specification asks for. Content.Library.ItemModel carries no JSON-Schema required list -- its create-time rules are stated per property, and docs/contract.json records the resulting classification. library_id and name must be provided, description and type are optional, and every other property is not used for the create operation and must not appear in the body. An optional argument left at None means 'not set': omit that property from the JSON entirely rather than sending null or an empty string. An empty string the caller passed explicitly is a value and must be sent. Note that item_type is the Python argument name while the wire property is type.

5. Read an item back. get_library_item() calls Content.Library.Item_get and returns the model as a dict.

mock/vcenter_mock.py is a loopback stand-in for vCenter that you can run while iterating. It builds its routes from docs/contract.json, so it serves those operations and nothing else, and it appends every request it receives to a JSONL log you can read. Run it with: python -m mock.vcenter_mock --port 8080 --log /tmp/requests.jsonl -- it prints the credentials and library id it accepts. Its --create-faults option controls how many create responses come back as a transient 503 before one succeeds.

python3 tests/verify_contract.py must pass. docs/, mock/ and tests/ are read-only; build the client to fit them.
